questions.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$  

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{x\cdot {\text{proj}}_{S}x}{‖x‖‖{\text{proj}}_{S}x‖} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 2+0\cdot (-2)+0\cdot 0}{\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{0}^{2}}\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{0}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{8}{\sqrt{16}\sqrt{8}} \\  & =\frac{8}{4\cdot 2\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2})=\frac{\pi }{4},
$$

which is already an acute angle.

questions.problem:
Find the acute angle between the vector $x$ and the subspace spanned by the linearly independent vectors $\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{8}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{4}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ Equivalently, it is the acute angle between $x$ and any non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,2\,{\text{proj}}_{S}x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].$

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{2\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot 1+1\cdot 2}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{6}\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{1}{2})=\frac{\pi }{3},
$$

which is already an acute angle.

questions.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}=0 \\ 4{x}_{1}-4{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the basis of the solution space of the system.

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to its row echelon form. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & -4 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}={x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 6{x}_{1}-12{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 6 & 0 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 5 \\ -8\end{aligned}],\,\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 4{x}_{1}+12{x}_{2}-12{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis for the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -3 & 0 \\ 4 & 12 & -12 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is $1$ pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}$ are free variables. Now, from the first equation, we get ${x}_{1}=-3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3}.$ Therefore, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3{x}_{2}+3{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2},\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B=\{[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}$ is the basis of the solution space of the system.

Now, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-20 \\ 5 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}10 & -9 \\ -9 & 10\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}65 \\ -68\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{19}[\begin{aligned}10 & 9 \\ 9 & 10\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}65 \\ -68\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-21 \\ 2 \\ -5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
